items.title: Nifty falls for sixth straight session; oil surge, CAS volatility rattle markets
items.description: Indian markets faced pressure as the Nifty declined for a sixth consecutive trading session. Rising oil prices and ongoing West Asia conflict kept traders cautious throughout the day. The Nifty closed lower, reflecting broader market weakness and investor concerns. Domestic institutional investors provided some buying support, while FPIs also bought shares. Technical indicators suggest a period of consolidation for the indices in the near term.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: The Nifty index continued its decline for a sixth consecutive session this week. Elevated crude oil prices and global tensions are impacting market sentiment negatively. Analysts anticipate continued pressure on Indian equities in the immediate future. Foreign and domestic institutional investors showed net buying activity on Tuesday. The Indian rupee closed slightly weaker due to oil prices and bond yields.

items.title: Stocks in news: ONGC, BPCL, RailTel Corporation, Exide Industries and Lohia Corp
items.description: The Indian stock market experienced a downward trend for the sixth consecutive session on Tuesday, influenced by rising oil prices and soaring global bond yields. Key companies like ONGC and BPCL will attract attention due to recent corporate developments. More newsworthy, RailTel Corporation and Compucom Software have landed significant contracts with government bodies. Additionally, Lohia Corp and others are expected to report their first-quarter earnings today.

items.title: India's outward FDI jumps 17% to $5.7 billion in July: RBI
items.description: India’s outward FDI rose 17% year-on-year to $5.70 billion in July from $4.88 billion a year earlier, according to provisional RBI data. It was also higher than the $3.14 billion recorded in June.

items.title: L&T Finance plans 500 new gold loan branches this fiscal
items.description: L&T Finance plans to open 500 new gold loan branches this financial year. This expansion aims to increase its network significantly and capitalize on sector growth. The company entered the gold loan market last year after acquiring Paul Merchants Finance. Gold loans are a key driver for L&T Finance's growth agenda.

items.title: Dividend alert! Mazagon Dock, Natco Pharma among 15 stocks turning ex-dividend on Thursday. Do you own any?
items.description: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders in April had announced that its board of directors have recommended a final dividend of Rs 4.62 per share for the financial year 2026. The company later fixed August 20 as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders set to receive the payment.

items.title: Negative Breakout: These 13 stocks cross below their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 13 stocks' close prices crossed below their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on August 18, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. Trading below the 200 DMA is considered a negative signal because it indicates that the stock's price is below its long-term trend line. The 200 DMA is used as a key indicator by traders for determining the overall trend in a particular stock. Take a look:

items.title: CCI approves Prudential’s stake acquisition in Bharti Life Insurance
items.description: The Competition Commission of India has approved Prudential Corporation of India’s acquisition of certain equity shareholding in Bharti Life Insurance Company. The transaction is still subject to other applicable regulatory and statutory approvals.

items.title: Milky Mist Dairy Foods lists at 18% premium to issue price
items.description: Mumbai-based Milky Mist Dairy Foods made a strong debut on the NSE, listing at ₹165—17.9% above its issue price of ₹140. The stock climbed further to close at the day’s high of ₹181.50, valuing the company at ₹13,972.66 crore at the close.

items.title: Tube Investments among 5 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On August 18, five Nifty500 stocks that gained over 3% were identified using the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” indicates that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is rising, suggesting strengthening price momentum in the stock. This may signal potential upward movement and can be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Behari Lal Engineering shares set to debut today; GMP signals 47% premium ahead of listing
items.description: The IPO, which was open for subscription from August 12 to August 14, drew an overwhelming response from investors and was subscribed 108.44 times overall. The retail portion was subscribed 53.27 times, while the QIB and NII categories saw exceptionally strong demand, with subscriptions of 165.33 times and 165.32 times, respectively.

items.title: Shiprocket shares to list today; GMP signals 37% listing gains
items.description: The Rs 1,617.48-crore IPO, which was open for subscription from August 12 to August 14, received an overwhelming response from investors. The issue was subscribed 99.38 times overall, reflecting exceptionally strong demand across investor categories.

items.title: Stocks to buy: 5 midcap and chemical stocks with up to 25% upside potential
items.description: Axis Securities in its latest report listed out five midcap and chemical stocks on which it recommends ‘Buy’ rating, as it believes they offer an attractive combination of earnings visibility, structural growth and improving operating performance, based on earnings assessment and medium-term outlook. “We believe companies with strong balance sheets, differentiated capabilities and execution track records are likely to gain market share as industry conditions improve,” it said. Here are the five stocks with their respective target prices and upside potentials.

items.title: Bosch among 4 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of August 18, there was a notable surge in futures open interest for four stocks in the NSE F&O pack, contributing to a total increase in open interest of over 10% as compared to the previous trade. A significant uptick in futures open interest signifies a substantial growth in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a specific security. This uptrend reflects an increasing number of participants either initiating new positions or expanding the size of their existing positions within the futures market.

items.title: Strong Q1 results spark stock-picking rush: 50 top ideas for investors to buy
items.description: The impressive earnings reported in the first quarter have led brokerages to unveil fresh stock-picking avenues. Investors are encouraged to seek out firms showcasing strong earnings and solid financial fundamentals. A collective effort from various brokerages has resulted in the identification of fifty prime stock options, covering diverse industries such as banking, automotive, and defense. The market is now pivoting towards an earnings-led cycle with an emphasis on quality companies.

items.title: Action Construction Equipment among 4 stocks flashing bullish signals, indicating possible uptrend
items.description: On August 18, four Nifty500 stocks that gained over 5% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: India Inc’s blockbuster Q1 earnings may not last as 3 key tailwinds fade in H2
items.description: India Inc's impressive earnings in the first quarter might not sustain their momentum into the latter half of the year. Diminishing effects from favorable base conditions and a slowdown in consumption stimulation are anticipated. Additionally, while a declining rupee and rising commodity costs have provided brief respite, analysts caution that profit growth could significantly slow down in the coming months, marking a stark contrast to the earlier strong performance.

items.title: D-Street’s CAS turmoil clouds BSE’s growth outlook
items.description: BSE shares have experienced a significant downturn this month following the launch of a new closing auction session. Since this change on August third, trading volumes and options activity have considerably dropped, raising concerns among analysts who have downgraded their outlook on the stock. The exchange is grappling with new funding rules and possible fee changes, but some analysts remain optimistic about a turnover rebound by October.

items.title: Sensex falls 100 points, Nifty below 23,150 as market bleeds for 7th session. What lies ahead?
items.description: On Wednesday morning, Indian stock markets faced further setbacks as both the Sensex and Nifty indices continued their downward trend, marking an ongoing losing streak. The broader market indices echoed this sentiment, showing substantial selling pressure. Notably, shares of Bajaj Finserv and Bajaj Finance led the decline on the Sensex, while IT stocks such as HCL Tech and Infosys managed to defy the overall trend by recording gains.

items.title: RailTel Corporation shares rally 5% after bagging Rs 166.8 crore EPFO order
items.description: RailTel shares gained nearly 5% after the company received a Rs 166.80 crore work order from EPFO for a one-year extension of its Infrastructure-as-a-Service engagement. While the order strengthens revenue and order-book visibility, technical indicators remain weak, with the stock trading below all 8 monitored SMAs and its RSI at 32.5. FII holding also rose modestly in the June 2026 quarter.

items.title: L&T Technology Services shares jump 3% after bagging $75 million deal
items.description: L&T Technology Services shares gained up to 3.3% after the engineering services company secured a five-year deal worth more than $75 million from a leading global technology enterprise. The mandate spans product engineering, software development, testing, digital engineering, and a dedicated Engineering Center. Technically, the stock remains in neutral territory, with short-term momentum improving but the longer-term trend awaiting confirmation.

items.title: Vijay Kedia buys Rs 33 crore stake in Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services via bulk deal, stock skyrockets 17%
items.description: Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services shares surged after Kedia Securities, owned by investor Vijay Kedia, acquired 20 lakh shares, or a 1.48% stake, through a bulk deal at Rs 164.72 apiece. The purchase came a day after the stock fell 20% following weak Q1 FY27 earnings.

items.title: Milky Mist shares hit another 10% upper circuit, rallying 43% from IPO price. Should you buy, sell or hold?
items.description: Milky Mist shares hit another 10% upper circuit on Wednesday, taking their gains to 42.5% from the IPO price of Rs 140. Analysts remain positive on the company’s strong foothold in value-added dairy products, improving margins and growth prospects, but caution that valuations are elevated. Existing investors have been advised to hold and accumulate on meaningful dips.

items.title: IT crash ahead? CLSA downgrades TCS, Infosys, Wipro, other stocks; revises target prices. Here's why
items.description: CLSA downgraded several large IT stocks and cut their target prices amid continued AI-related concerns, while retaining a bullish view on select mid-tier IT companies. The brokerage said Q1 earnings were mixed across Indian IT and global peers, but expects AI-driven volumes to eventually offset pricing deflation by FY30.

items.title: HG Infra Engineering shares jump over 8% after receiving LoI from REC
items.description: HG Infra Engineering shares rose after the company received a letter of intent from REC Power Development and Consultancy for constructing two 220/132/33 kV AIS substations and associated transmission lines in Uttar Pradesh.

items.title: Shiprocket shares soar 10% after bumper market debut, rally 48% from IPO price. Time to buy or sell?
items.description: Shiprocket shares extended their post-listing rally, after making a strong debut at a 35% premium to the IPO price. The stock touched Rs 144, taking its gains from the issue price to over 48%. Analysts advised allotted investors to book some profits, while fresh investors should wait for dips.

items.title: IGL, MGL, Adani Total Gas shares rally up to 6% as govt boosts domestic PNG push
items.description: City gas distributor stocks rallied after the government approved an incentive scheme to accelerate domestic PNG connections from September 1. Mahanagar Gas, IGL, Adani Total Gas rose as the scheme aims to expand active piped gas connections and promote cleaner, safer and affordable cooking fuel.

items.title: India stocks top Indonesia as Asia’s least-favoured in BofA poll
items.description: India has replaced Indonesia as Asia’s least-preferred stock market among fund managers surveyed by Bank of America, with 32% of respondents net underweight on Indian equities. Lack of clear AI exposure, weak growth, high valuations and limited reforms emerged as key concerns, even as improving earnings and renewed foreign inflows provide some support.

items.title: Time to take some risk, but with guardrails? 5 small-cap stocks with an upside potential of up to 30%
items.description: With oil prices going past $91 a barrel yet again, expect volatility to keep hitting the markets. The contradictory claims by the US and Iran on everything from peace talks to whether the Strait of Hormuz is open or not only makes matters worse. In such a scenario, should investors just wait and watch? Not necessarily. There are segments of the market to which they can take exposure – provided, of course, they have a long-term horizon.

items.title: BSE shares bounce 2% after 5-session losing streak. Here’s why Jefferies, Nuvama advise caution
items.description: BSE shares face fresh pressure after Nuvama and Jefferies downgraded the stock, citing headwinds from the Closing Auction Session, RBI’s bank guarantee norms and limited scope for further market share gains. Nuvama cut its target price to Rs 3,240, while Jefferies lowered its target to Rs 2,940.

items.title: Jefferies cuts target price for Jupiter Wagons, maintains Underperform after Q1 earnings. Here’s why
items.description: Jefferies has cut its target price for Jupiter Wagons to Rs 185 from Rs 210 and retained its Underperform rating after weak Q1 earnings. The brokerage lowered FY27E-29E EPS estimates by 6%-20%, citing weaker wagon and wheelset sales, margin pressure and slower execution, while maintaining a positive view on the company’s long-term wheel manufacturing opportunity.

items.title: Volume Shocker: MFs added 1 crore+ shares to 8 stocks in July '26; rally up to 76%
items.description: In its latest mutual fund analysis, ETMarkets highlighted the stocks that witnessed the largest increase in mutual fund holdings in July 2026 compared with June 2026. The report revealed that 58 stocks recorded net additions of more than 1 crore shares each, indicating strong buying interest from mutual fund houses.To identify the most promising opportunities from this list, we applied a second filter, focusing on stocks that not only witnessed significant mutual fund accumulation but also delivered gains in the range of 10-76 per cent since the beginning of July. This two-step screening narrowed the universe to eight standout stocks, reflecting both strong institutional demand and robust market performance.

items.title: Fabrinet stock plunges 19%: Why investors are selling after Q4 beat
items.description: Fabrinet plunged 19.4% on August 18, sharply underperforming the broader market after investors reacted negatively to the company’s fiscal Q4 results and outlook. The stock had closed at $598.58 on Monday before the sell-off. (Sources: The Motley Fool, Investing.com)

items.title: Behari Lal Engineering shares rally 14% after stellar debut. What are brokerages saying?
items.description: Behari Lal Engineering shares surged 14% after making a strong market debut, listing at a 63% premium to the IPO price. Brokerages remain positive, citing strong investor appetite and reasonable valuations, though they advise investors to book partial profits after the sharp listing gains. Here’s what SBI Securities and Swastika Investmart recommend on the stock.

items.title: BlackRock, Capital Group anchor IDFC FIRST Bank’s maiden $500 million global bond
items.description: IDFC FIRST Bank raised $500 million through its maiden international bond issuance, marking its entry into global debt markets. The three-year senior notes, due in 2029, carry a 5.625% coupon and attracted major investors including BlackRock, Capital Group and AllianceBernstein. The fundraising diversifies the bank’s funding base and supports its long-term growth ambitions.

items.title: Indian Bank raises $400 million for four years
items.description: Indian Bank raised $400 million through a four-year overseas funding programme via its GIFT City branch, joining Indian lenders tapping global debt markets. Banks are accelerating dollar bond issuances following regulatory changes to the concessional swap window for FCNR deposits. Axis, ICICI, Federal, IDFC First, Kotak Mahindra and Yes Bank are also active.

items.title: Swiggy to see $400 million outflows after Indian-owned status? Jefferies explains why
items.description: Swiggy is moving closer to becoming an Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC), a move that could enable an inventory-led model for Instamart and potentially improve margins. However, Jefferies expects the shift to trigger passive outflows of over $400 million from MSCI and FTSE indices due to foreign ownership limits. The brokerage retained its Buy rating with a target price of Rs 435.

items.title: Sebi to soon roll out AI rules with a ‘kill switch’ for stock market
items.description: Sebi will soon issue guidelines for responsible AI and machine learning use in India’s securities market, with mandatory safeguards including a “kill switch”, human oversight and data controls. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the framework will balance innovation with investor protection as AI adoption expands across surveillance, risk assessment, fraud detection and investor servicing, while ensuring accountability among regulated entities.

items.title: Oil India vs ONGC vs OMCs: What JM Financial’s $80 Brent call means for oil stocks
items.description: Brent crude may stay near eighty dollars a barrel for twelve months.  Analysts favor Oil India and ONGC due to expected earnings growth.  Oil India's refinery capacity expansion will drive future output increases.  Oil marketing companies face pressure from lower integrated gross margins.  Valuation and earnings concerns persist for HPCL, BPCL, and IOCL.

items.title: Market wrap:  HCL Tech, Sun Pharma, Power Grid, Bajaj Finance top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Wednesday
items.description: Indian equities extended losses for a seventh session, with Nifty falling 0.32% and Sensex 0.42% ahead of US FOMC minutes. IT stocks gained, but broader markets weakened. Analysts flagged 24,000 as crucial Nifty support amid persistent sell-on-rallies sentiment.

items.title: Tech holds the crown, but defensive positioning grows: BofA survey
items.description: Technology remains investors’ top choice, but Asia fund managers are turning defensive, with 59% hedging AI downside through value, cyclical and defensive sectors. Asia ex-Japan optimism rose, while Japan exposure remains concentrated in banks and semiconductors amid policy expectations and weaker semiconductor sentiment.

items.title: Lenskart Solutions among 4 stocks to hit 52-week highs & surge up to 25% in a month
items.description: On Wednesday, the benchmark Sensex fell 325 points to close at 76,909. Despite the broader market weakness, four stocks from the BSE 200 Index touched fresh 52-week highs, marking their strongest price levels in the past year. A 52-week high is generally considered a positive technical indicator, reflecting strong investor interest, improving market sentiment, and the potential for further upward momentum.

items.title: Rs 3 crore to Rs 4,925 crore: Sebi order gives details on Dhenu Buildcon market cap surge
items.description: Sebi’s interim order alleges Dhenu Buildcon routed Rs 1,000 crore through connected entities as loans, later converting Rs 840 crore into equity. Despite negligible revenue, its market cap surged to Rs 4,925 crore. The regulator ordered restrictions while investigations continue.

items.title: BSE looks to launch MSCI-linked futures and options in India
items.description: BSE has partnered with MSCI to explore futures and options contracts linked to MSCI indexes in India, subject to regulatory approvals. The move could broaden BSE’s derivatives offerings, strengthen index-based investing and provide investors additional tools to hedge India exposure.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A top EMS company for a 8.5% gain, a mid-cap IT stock for an almost 7% rise
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Sebi flags manipulative trades during CAS on Sensex expiry day, fines two entities
items.description: Sebi issued an interim order against Copthall Mauritius and Mansi Share and Stock Broking for manipulative trading during the August 13, 2026, Closing Auction Session. The regulator impounded Rs 3.67 crore in alleged wrongful gains from these two entities.

items.title: Goldman Sachs backs D-street debutante Shiprocket, buys over 40 lakh shares
items.description: Shiprocket debuted on the NSE at ₹131, a 35% premium, closing at ₹143.10. Goldman Sachs India EQ Portfolio acquired 40.24 lakh shares post-listing. Analysts advise investors to book partial profits while holding remaining shares for long-term growth.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Thursday
items.description: Indian equities extended losses for a seventh session as rising oil prices and US-Iran tensions heightened risk aversion. Nifty fell to 24,078, while Sensex declined 326 points. Analysts flagged 24,000-24,050 as crucial support, with weak breadth favouring bears.

items.title: Stock Radar: Bata India stock showing signs of bottoming out, but wait for a break above 750 levels
items.description: Bata India stock shows signs of a potential bottom formation after a significant fall. Experts suggest buying the stock for a bounce back towards 800 levels. The stock has found strong support in the Rs 620–680 zone recently. A sustained close above Rs 750 could strengthen the recovery and open the way. Traders can buy on dips around Rs 735–720 with a stop loss below Rs 710.
